### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-dev`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via DevPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 31 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a2494a766d181180d84e11c745f0966212b76daa` — the merge of head `c2db30e78717c3237cef19631fc77bf6dc95091c` into base `0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a2494a766d181180d84e11c745f0966212b76daa && git checkout a2494a766d181180d84e11c745f0966212b76daa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02 c2db30e78717c3237cef19631fc77bf6dc95091c && git checkout -B drift-repro 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02 && git merge --no-ff c2db30e78717c3237cef19631fc77bf6dc95091c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2db30e78717c3237cef19631fc77bf6dc95091c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23310 (body, triage `6151745744`, claim `6177340429`, dev report `6179980256`), PR #23550 (body, 12-file list, net diff against merge-base `5fd2c76d6` of `main`), and the check-runs on the head, read once. Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head (read once at review time).** Completed `success`: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, the four PR-claim guards, filter. Completed `skipped` (path-gated): Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. **Still in progress at brief time:** Build Core; Test Core (1/6 … 6/6); Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus. No watcher was set; the adopting seat reads their conclusions before the queue. Nothing completed is red.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **New `@objectstack/core` export `stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(stack: unknown, plugins: readonly unknown[] = []): boolean`** (`packages/core/src/stack-organization-record-page.ts`, re-exported from `packages/core/src/index.ts`). Item by item:
   - *Name:* names the fact it reads (the served stack declares an organization record page), not an outcome or a switch. **Right.**
   - *Input:* the stack the root serves, plus the root's own `plugins` list; both typed `unknown`, so a config module, a `defineStack` output, a multi-package stack and a bundle all pass. **Right.**
   - *What it reads:* `pages` off the stack by `resolveStackCollection`'s rule (top-level `pages` when the key is carried, otherwise each package body's, ADR-0130 D4), and `pages` off each `plugins[]` entry that exposes a `bundle` object, by the same rule; each page judged by `defaultRecordPageObject(page) === SystemObjectName.ORGANIZATION`. `defaultRecordPageObject` (`packages/spec/src/ui/default-record-page.ts`) is the one reading every refusal door uses (isDefault exactly `true`, type `record` or absent, non-empty `object`), so the predicate cannot say yes to a page the registry would not count as a default. **Right.**
   - *Single yes/no on a declared fact, no ordering or precedence rule (ruling A on #23015 as the card and triage render it):* the body is `bundles.some(... .some(...))`; the answer is invariant under any permutation of `plugins` and of `pages`, and no page outranks another. When it answers `true`, `plugin-auth`'s page is composed out; a second default from any other source is still refused by the registry naming both. This is exactly the second spelling the card itself offered ("deriving it when the app's own stack declares a default record page for `sys_organization`"), and triage left the choice to the measurement. **Right.**
   - *Failure shape:* a malformed `packages[]` on a stack with no top-level `pages` raises the collection reader's `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES`, the same refusal the boot raises when it registers that stack, and the predicate does not swallow it. Declared in the TSDoc `@throws`. **Right.**
   - *Dependency direction:* core already depends on `@objectstack/spec` (`packages/core/package.json`), `./ui` and `./system` are published subpaths of spec, and core already imports `@objectstack/spec/system` at runtime in eight modules; this is the first runtime import of `@objectstack/spec/ui` in core, placed in its own file rather than `stack-auth.ts`. Neither `cli` nor `plugin-dev` can import the other, both already import core. **Right.**
   - *One note, not a defect:* the `plugins` leg reads `AppPlugin`'s `bundle`, which `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:152` declares `private bundle: any`. The read is structural at runtime and works (the e2e boot and the contract pin's plain-object shape prove it), but the coupling is undeclared on `AppPlugin`'s side. Follow-up: a public readonly accessor on `AppPlugin`, or a comment on the field naming this reader. Not a must-fix: on both roots the stack itself is also passed, so the config boot's answer does not depend on this leg.

2. **`os serve` (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`)** — the single `new AuthPlugin(` construction (line ~3999, step 5d) now passes `registerOrganizationRecordPage: !stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(config, plugins)`. `plugins` is declared at ~3029 (`stackBootPlugins(config, flags.dev)`), the `new AppPlugin(config)` wrap is appended at ~3369 (step 3), and `stackSuppliesAuthPlugin(plugins)` at ~3884 still skips the construction when the host composes its own `AuthPlugin`, so a host that sets the option by hand keeps it. The predicate therefore runs before `AuthPlugin` is constructed, over the config and the app wrap(s). **Right.** The import is added to the existing `@objectstack/core` import block. **Right.**

3. **`DevPlugin` (`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin.ts`)** — step 3 wraps `this.options.stack` in `AppPlugin` (line ~569); step 4 constructs `AuthPlugin` (line ~715) with `registerOrganizationRecordPage: !stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(this.options.stack)`. `DevPluginOptions` carries `stack?` and no plugin list of its own, so the one-argument call reads everything the root composes. **Right.** *Same stack, same answer under both roots:* both read the same `pages` by the same rule through the same function; serve's extra `plugins` leg only adds the wrap over that same config (or host-composed `AppPlugin`s that `DevPlugin` cannot carry at all). **Right.**

4. **`DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` remedy (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:~1783`)** — "or compose the deployment without the package that ships the other" becomes "or compose the deployment without the other package's page". It names no option, no package, no tracker number (triage `6151745744`); code, `422`, the named pages and the first and last sentences are unchanged. The TSDoc above the class is reworded to match and says why the page, not the package, is named. **Right.** The card asked for "without that package's page"; "the other package's page" is the same step in the sentence's own frame of two named pages. **Right.**

5. **Every pin of the old sentence moved?** At the head the old sentence survives only in: four `CHANGELOG.md` files and `.changeset/pre/23015-…md` (release records, not this PR's to edit), and `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:1671` (item 6b). No test at the head asserts the old registry sentence; the existing registry pins read `message.split('. ')[0]` and are untouched; the new case in `registry-default-record-page.test.ts` asserts the new sentence verbatim and the absence of `without the package`, `#NNN`, `registerOrganizationRecordPage` and `plugin-auth`. `default-record-page-save-door.test.ts:191` pins the *metadata-protocol* sentence, which this PR does not change, so it stays green by construction. **Right: nothing left half-moved.**

6. **The two out-of-scope findings the dev noted, not filed:**
   - (a) `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `saveMetaItem` remedy (`protocol.ts:~21275`): "a page a package ships stays the default unless the deployment is composed without that package". This is a different door (metadata save) with its own holder model, and this PR changes nothing about what that door accepts. The sentence was already too narrow after PR #23309 (a host can leave out the page, not the package); this PR widens the set of deployments for which it is too narrow but does not make a statement that was true false. **A sibling of the old wording, a follow-up, not a must-fix.** It is pinned verbatim by `default-record-page-save-door.test.ts:191`, so its move is a change with its own pin to carry.
   - (b) `PageSchema.isDefault` TSDoc (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:1670–1672`): "To change which page opens: set `isDefault: false` on one of the two, or compose the deployment without the package that ships the other." Author-facing prose; still a true statement of one way (a host composing its own kernel can drop a package), and it does not deny the path this PR adds. **A sibling, a follow-up, not a must-fix.** A third sibling the dev did not list: the source comment at `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:919–920` ("composing the deployment without the other package"), comment-only, same follow-up.
   - Neither is a stale *published* statement this PR makes false; the one published runtime text this card named, the registry remedy, is moved. The dev's "carrier: none" is accepted; the adopting seat may file one follow-up card for the three siblings together.

7. **`packages/cli/src/utils/boot-preparation-parity.test.ts`** — one `SERVE_ONLY` row for `stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage`, with the reason: the `os migrate` one-shot boot composes `plugin-auth`'s objects through `createIdentityObjectsPlugin` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-objects-plugin.ts`), which registers no page (confirmed: the module names no page), so it has no organization page to leave out. **Right**, and the surface widening to this file is the pin reddening on the new import, not a design choice.

8. **Pins and negative controls (the card's third ask):** `packages/core/src/stack-organization-record-page.test.ts` (yes/no pairs over top-level pages, untyped page, package body, app bundle; controls for `isDefault: false`, absent, other object, `home` page, empty, `undefined`); `packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin-organization-record-page.test.ts` (recording `AuthPlugin`; `false` with the page, `true` with `isDefault: false`, no pages, no stack); `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-auth-organization-record-page.contract.test.ts` (exactly one `new AuthPlugin(` in `serve.ts`, carrying the derived option; the predicate over an `AppPlugin`-shaped bundle with an `isDefault: false` control); `packages/cli/test/serve-organization-record-page.e2e.test.ts` (two real `os serve` boots, the app page is the single default vs. plugin-auth's page as the control, `sys_user` read in both so exactly one page moves); `registry-default-record-page.test.ts` new remedy case. Each pin has its negative control, as the card lists. **Right.**

Nothing in the diff is judged wrong.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23310-serve-org-record-page.md`: `@objectstack/core` **minor** (a new public export), `@objectstack/cli` **minor** (`os serve` now boots an app shape it refused: an app declaring its own `sys_organization` default), `@objectstack/plugin-dev` **minor** (same widening for `DevPlugin`), `@objectstack/objectql` **patch** (the remedy sentence of an existing error; code, status and named pages unchanged). All four are in the `fixed` group, so they version together regardless; the per-package levels still describe what each publishes correctly. The changeset body states the new export by name and signature, the derived rule, the unchanged default, and "nothing to adopt". `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset, `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body, matching the claim. Check Changeset is green on the head. **Right; `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.**

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the accept set of `os serve` and `DevPlugin` widens by one declared app shape, through a new core export; no stack-config key is added, so no spec authorable surface, no liveness row and no generated baseline move.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: `[]` — nothing to answer.

Dev deviations, each answered:
1. *Surface widened to `packages/core` and `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts`.* The claim's own term ("the stack-config schema in `packages/spec/src/**` only if the measurement picks forwarding") shows the surface was expected to follow the measurement; derive needs one shared predicate and core is the only package both roots depend on (①.1). The parity row is a pin going red on the new import (①.7). **Accepted.**
2. *The `os serve` pin is a nightly-tier e2e (two real boots, ~28 s against a 10 s per-file budget).* Is the unit-tier contract pin enough per-PR guard? Per PR, the chain is covered in three unit pins: the predicate's own truth table (core), `DevPlugin`'s recorded option (plugin-dev), the single `serve.ts` construction carrying `!stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage(config, plugins)` (cli contract pin), and `plugin-auth` already pins what `false` does on a real kernel (`organization-record-page-option.test.ts`, unchanged). What only the e2e proves is the composition of all four in one real `os serve` process, and that belongs in the real-boot tier by this package's own tiering rule (`vitest.config.ts`, `OS_TEST_TIERS`, #16455). The source-text pin is brittle only loudly: moving the construction into a helper reds it rather than silently losing the guard. **Enough; accepted.**
3. *Changeset levels and Clause-② spelling.* Judged in ②. **Accepted.**
4. *Zero label writes.* The dispatch named none. **Accepted.**
5. *Commit trailers model-free.* Outside this record's surface; nothing to judge.

Out-of-scope findings (two noted, not filed): judged in ①.6 as follow-ups, with a third sibling added; no must-fix.

Check-runs in progress at brief time are named above; none is escalated, since every completed run is green and the brief forbids a watcher.

Landing waits on the in-progress check families finishing green on this head.
